newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish pound firms on mark and stg, focus on EMU.
newsitem.headline: Irish pound firms on mark and stg, focus on EMU.

text.p: The Irish pound settled above 2.60 against the mark on Wednesday, prodded on by EMU jitters which sparked some closing off of short positions in the Irish unit, dealers said.
The Irish pound gained on sterling which dipped against the dollar and mark after UK unemployment fell less than forecast in May to 5.8 percent.
By 11.01 GMT, the Irish pound firmed to 2.6050 marks up from a close of 2.6031 marks. The Irish unit was trading at 0.9275 stg up from 0.9248 stg.

"Generally there is an appetite to buy Irish pounds," one currency dealer said. "There are a lot of short positions in the Irish pound in relation to EMU and it doesn't take much to incite nervousness on that score."
The dealer said a media report and market talk that prime minister-elect Bertie Ahern had hinted at delaying Ireland's entry into Europe added to nervousness at the open.
But a spokesman for Ireland's newly-elected government later denied that the government was considering a delay in Ireland's EMU membership.
"There has been no change in our stance. Bertie Ahern has said and still maintains that Ireland will enter EMU at the start date if we qualify," a spokesman for Ahern told Reuters.
Bertie Ahern's new Fianna Fail/Progressive Democrat alliance, which polled two seats short of a majority in a June 6 poll, is expected to have a new government in place by the weekend.

Ahern will be formally voted in as prime minister when parliament reconvenes on June 26 and in the meantime the defeated centre-left 'Rainbow Coalition' of Prime Minister John Bruton will form a caretaker administration until then.
